paragraphs.en: Like most of us, I try to be {mindful} of food that goes to waste.The arugula ( (芝麻菜) ) was to make a {nice} green salad, {rounding} out a {roast} {chicken} dinner.But I ended up working late.Then friends called with a dinner invitation.I stuck the chicken in the {freezer} .But as days passed, the arugula went bad.Even {worse} , I was too {greedy} and {unthinkingly} bought {way} too much; I could have made six salads with what I threw out.This fact made my {cheeks} burn with shame.
paragraphs.cn: 和我们大多数人一样，我尽量 <u> 留意 </u> 避免食物被浪费。我本来要用芝麻菜做一个 <u> 美味的 </u> 绿色沙拉， <u> 搭配烤鸡 </u> 晚餐。但最后我工作到很晚，然后朋友们又打电话邀请我共进晚餐。我就把鸡肉塞进了 <u> 冷冻柜 </u> 。但是，几天过去，芝麻菜变质了。 <u> 更糟糕 </u> 的是，我当时太 <u> 贪心 </u> ， <u> 不假思索地 </u> 买了太多的芝麻菜。我扔掉的这些芝麻菜够做六份沙拉了。这一事实让我羞愧得 <u> 脸颊 </u> 发烫。

paragraphs.en: In a world where {nearly} 800 million people a year go hungry,“food waste goes against the moral {grain} ,”as Elizabeth Royte writes in this month's cover story.Anyone would {choke} on the stark statistics showing how much {perfectly} good food is thrown away—from“ {ugly} ”(but quite {eatable} ) {pears} rejected by {grocers} to large amounts of {uneaten} {dishes} thrown into restaurant {garbage} {cans} .The issue of food waste is no longer something we can afford to {suspend} from our immediate attention.
paragraphs.cn: 在一个每年有 <u> 近 </u> 8亿人挨饿的世界里，正如伊丽莎白·罗伊特在本月的封面故事中所写的那样：“食物浪费违背了道德 <u> 常理 </u> 。”任何人看到这些赤裸裸的统计数据都会感到 <u> 窒息 </u> ，这些数据显示了有多少 <u> 完 </u> 好的食物被丢弃——从被 <u> 杂货商 </u> 拒之门外的“ <u> 卖相不好 </u> ”（但完全 <u> 能吃 </u> ）的 <u> 梨 </u> ，到大量被倒进餐馆 <u> 垃圾桶 </u> 的 <u> 未吃完的菜肴 </u> 。食物浪费问题已不再是我们能够暂且 <u> 搁置 </u> 、不立刻关注的事情了。

paragraphs.en: The production of food like {pork} and {beef} involves intensive farming practices.Producing food that {no} one eats wastes water and {fuel} .The transportation of these {goods} also involves burning {petrol} and emitting greenhouse gases.That makes food waste an environmental problem.In fact, Royte writes,“if food waste were a country, it would be the third-largest {producer} of {greenhouse} gases in the world.”
paragraphs.cn: 像 <u> 猪肉 </u> 和 <u> 牛肉 </u> 这类食品的生产涉及集约化的养殖方式。生产 <u> 无 </u> 人食用的食物会浪费水和 <u> 燃料 </u> 。运输这些 <u> 货物 </u> 的过程还会燃烧 <u> 汽油 </u> ，排放温室气体。这使食物浪费成为一个环境问题。事实上，罗伊特写道：“如果把食物浪费比作一个国家，那么它将是世界上第三大 <u> 温室 </u> 气体 <u> 排放国 </u> 。”

paragraphs.en: If that's hard to {understand} , let's keep it as simple as the arugula at the back of my {refrigerator} .Mike Curtin sees my arugula story all the time—but for {him} , it's more like {twelve} boxes of {donated} {strawberries} {nearing} their last days.Curtin is {CEO} of DC {Central} {Kitchen} in Washington, D.C., which {recovers} food and turns it into healthy meals.Last year it recovered more than 807,500 pounds of food by taking {donations} and {collecting} blemished ( (有瑕疵的) ) produce that otherwise would have rotted in fields.And the strawberries? Volunteers will {wash} , cut, and {freeze} or dry them for use in meals down the road.
paragraphs.cn: 如果这很难 <u> 理解 </u> ，那就让我们把问题简单化，就拿我 <u> 冰箱 </u> 深处的芝麻菜来举例。迈克·科廷看到我的“芝麻菜故事”每天不断地在重演——但对 <u> 他 </u> 来说，这种情况更像是 <u> 十二 </u> 箱 <u> 临近 </u> 保质期的 <u> 捐赠草莓 </u> 。科廷是华盛顿特区 <u> 中央厨房 </u> 的 <u> 首席执行官 </u> ，这家机构 <u> 回收 </u> 食物，并将其制作成健康的餐食。去年，通过接受 <u> 捐赠 </u> 、 <u> 收集 </u> 那些原本会腐烂在田里的有瑕疵的农产品，该机构回收了超过807500磅的食品。那么那些草莓呢？志愿者们会将它们 <u> 清洗 </u> 、切割，然后 <u> 冷冻 </u> 或烘干，以备日后用于制作餐食。

paragraphs.en: In countries like {Japan} and {Canada} , innovative approaches are being adopted to reduce food waste.For example, some apps connect consumers with extra food from local restaurants and {pubs} .Environmental {ministers} in some countries have even started to {tax} food waste.
paragraphs.cn: <u> 日本 </u> 、 <u> 加拿大 </u> 等国家正在采用创新方法来减少食物浪费。例如，一些应用程序将消费者和当地餐馆和 <u> 酒吧 </u> 的剩余餐食联系起来。有些国家的环境 <u> 部长 </u> 甚至开始 <u> 对 </u> 食物浪费行为 <u> 征税 </u> 。

paragraphs.en: Such methods seem obvious, yet so often we just don't think.“Everyone can play a part in reducing waste, whether by not purchasing more food than necessary in your weekly {shopping} or by asking restaurants not to include the side dish you won't eat,”Curtin says.
paragraphs.cn: 这些方法看似显而易见，但我们常常不以为然。科廷说：“每个人都可以在减少浪费方面发挥作用，无论是在每周 <u> 购物 </u> 时不买超出所需的食物，还是要求餐馆不提供你不吃的配菜。” 5NoOncib/NjiX02BpMIzP4m+378Hw1xTRxUdPaP/PFjKUFq4K2G7tp6ZLYoCE601yW1W39VMdLmovFdSHs4nVQ==
